subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should OpenClaw grant operator scopes to device-less shared-token/password WebSocket clients, and if so should that happen through configured token scopes, a device-bound trust flow, or not at all?
rationale: Current main, docs, and tests intentionally clear self-declared scopes for this class of client, while the reported workflow needs write-capable remote/headless operators; changing that boundary is a security/product choice, not a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Bound Configured Token Scopes
options.body: Land a reviewed tokenScopes-style policy that grants only configured scopes with explicit network/admin safety bounds and regression proof.

options.title: Require Device Identity
options.body: Keep device-less shared-token clients scope-empty and document that remote/headless operators must use device tokens or pairing to obtain write/admin scopes.

options.title: Preserve Client-Declared Scopes
options.body: Allow successful shared-token/password clients to retain requested scopes, accepting the larger shared-secret trust boundary after explicit maintainer approval.

recommendation.title: Bound Configured Token Scopes
recommendation.body: Land a reviewed tokenScopes-style policy that grants only configured scopes with explicit network/admin safety bounds and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the current tokenScopes implementation candidate and has recent history on the affected Gateway auth/config surface.
